title: Jailed Istanbul Mayor İmamoğlu Sentenced to Over 2 Years in Separate Insult Case
detail: An Istanbul court sentenced jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu to 2 years and 1 month in prison for publicly insulting former Tuzla district mayor Şadi Yazıcı, in a retrial of a case dating to an October 25, 2022 wastewater plant opening where İmamoğlu called Yazıcı's conduct 'discourteous.' İmamoğlu had won two prior acquittals in the same case before an appeals court ordered a retrial on procedural grounds. The court also imposed an Article 53 political ban restricting his ability to hold public office; the ban and prison term are not immediately enforceable and take effect only if upheld on appeal. İmamoğlu called the ruling invalid, saying 'appointed judges cannot decide my fate.' The conviction is separate from — and adds to — the mass corruption trial with 412 co-defendants that has been underway since March 2026, in which prosecutors are seeking 2,430+ years, and a parallel espionage indictment.

title: Erdoğan Refers to 'Approaching Elections' in First Public Hint at Early Vote
detail: Speaking to supporters in his family's hometown of Güneysu (Rize province), President Erdoğan said 'with God's will, I once again believe that we will definitely win the upcoming election' — the first time he has publicly characterized Turkey's next election as 'approaching' rather than reaffirming the scheduled May 14, 2028 date. He did not name a specific date or explicitly call for early elections. Under Article 116 of the constitution, a president who has served two terms becomes eligible to run again only if parliament — not the president — calls early elections during the second term; AKP and ally MHP hold roughly 326-328 of the 600 seats, short of the 360 needed. Opposition leader Özgür Özel responded that voters would 'change the government' rather than let Erdoğan 'get through' any election.

media.caption: President Erdoğan speaks to supporters in Güneysu, hinting at 'approaching elections'
